headline: GOLIATH CONFIRMS VOLCANIC WEDGE ZONES BRIDGE BONANZA AND GOLDEN GATE GOLD TARGETS — 7 Rigs, 50,000m Program Expands Combined 2.68 km² Footprint In British Columbia's Golden Triangle
snippet: Goliath Resources Limited (TSX-V: GOT) released August 31 drill results from its Golddigger Property in British Columbia's Golden Triangle confirming newly defined volcanic Wedge Zones — broad intervals of gold-bearing quartz-sulphide mineralization with visible gold — connecting the Bonanza and Golden Gate zones in a configuration that opens the potential for large-scale bulk-tonnage extraction between the two formerly separate high-grade targets. The Golden Gate Zone footprint has grown from 0.85 km² to 1.17 km² (38% expansion) and the Bonanza Zone from 1.27 km² to 1.51 km² (19% expansion), both remaining open laterally and at depth. Seven drill rigs and approximately 50,000 metres of systematic drilling are budgeted for the fully funded 2026 programme. The high-grade Surebet Discovery continues to be tested concurrently. For retail investors: the Wedge Zone result is architecturally significant — it suggests Bonanza and Golden Gate may form a single larger mineralized system rather than two discrete targets, the kind of geometry that can re-rate a project from a high-grade niche story to a large-tonnage development candidate.

headline: BUNKER HILL CATE-8 VEIN RETURNS 14m AT 166 g/t AgEq — Individual Samples Hit 16.3 oz/ton Silver And 41.1% Lead As Silver47 Merger Validates Idaho Asset Quality
snippet: Bunker Hill Mining Corp. (TSX: BNKR) released August 31 assay results from its ongoing underground exploration programme at the Bunker Hill Mine in Idaho's Silver Valley, intersecting additional high-grade silver in the Cate-8 Vein. Underground channel sampling returned 14.03 metres at 166 g/t silver-equivalent (4.83 oz/ton AgEq: 8.19% lead, 2.49 oz/ton silver, 1.18% zinc) across 46 feet of strike, with individual drill samples reaching 16.3 oz/ton silver and 41.1% lead. The best combined interval came in at 24.43 oz/ton silver-equivalent (837.74 g/t AgEq). The results land as the company advances its definitive arrangement agreement to acquire Silver47 Exploration (announced August 21) for approximately $163 million in an all-share transaction designed to create a 'Made in America' US silver and critical minerals champion. The Cate-8 Vein results confirm the quality of Bunker Hill's Idaho Silver Valley asset base ahead of shareholder votes on the merger, reinforcing the strategic rationale for combining operating production with Silver47's Alaska, Nevada and New Mexico exploration pipeline.

headline: INDEPENDENCE GOLD PROVES GOOFY VEIN CONTINUES 30m BELOW DISCOVERY — 9.23m AT 5.12 g/t Au AND 33 g/t Ag Extends British Columbia High-Grade At Depth
snippet: Independence Gold Corp. (CSE: IGO) released August 31 follow-up drill results from the recently discovered Goofy Vein at its 100%-owned 3Ts Gold Project in British Columbia's Nechako Plateau, 185 km southwest of Prince George. Drill hole 3TS-26-48 intersected 9.23 metres at 5.12 g/t gold and 33.04 g/t silver — approximately 30 metres below the original Goofy discovery intercept (July 22: 9.10 metres at 14.70 g/t gold and 36.70 g/t silver). The result confirms the Goofy Vein has meaningful vertical continuity, a critical characteristic that differentiates a drill-hole anomaly from a mineable vein. The 3Ts Project covers 35,486 hectares on the Nechako Plateau and hosts multiple vein systems; the Goofy Vein was discovered 250 metres west of the existing Ted-Mint Vein System. At current gold prices above $4,400, a vein system returning 14+ g/t at surface and 5+ g/t at 30 metres depth carries the grade characteristics to support a narrow-vein underground mining scenario. The project property comprises 31 mineral claims and drilling continues.

headline: VIZSLA COPPER EXPANDS PALMER DRILL PROGRAM AFTER HG PROSPECT VMS DISCOVERY — Zone 1 Success And New Alaska Mineralization Drive Programme Upsize
snippet: Vizsla Copper Corp. (TSX-V: VCU) announced August 31 an expansion of its 2026 diamond drill programme at the Palmer Copper-Zinc VMS Project in Southeast Alaska following two near-simultaneous exploration successes. At the HG Prospect — located 600 metres west of the main Palmer Deposit along the same geological corridor — drilling returned the discovery of new mineralization that will drive follow-up holes as part of the expanded programme. Simultaneously, the first drill hole of the expanded programme at the AG Deposit intersected a broad mineralized system containing multiple intervals of semi-massive, massive and barite-bearing sulphide mineralization. Palmer's primary deposit is a high-grade copper-zinc-silver VMS system sharing geological characteristics with the HG Prospect; the 600-metre strike between them represents significant district-scale potential. Volcanogenic massive sulphide discoveries typically cluster along stratigraphic horizons — a confirmed second mineralized zone 600 metres from the main deposit implies the Palmer corridor is more fertile than the original resource outline suggested. For copper-focused investors: Palmer's Alaskan jurisdiction, VMS geology, and now dual-zone exploration profile position it in a supply-scarce copper market.

headline: GOLDERA TARGETS SYENITE-HOSTED GOLD IN TIMMINS CAMP AND ACADIAN GOLD JV IN NEW BRUNSWICK — Geophysics And Channel Sampling Precede Q3/Q4 Drill Test At Egan
snippet: Goldera Exploration Ltd. provided August 31 updates on two active 2026 exploration programmes. At the Egan Gold Property — located 35 km west of Timmins in the prolific Abitibi-Greenstone Belt — the company is advancing a syenite-hosted gold system that represents an emerging discovery style for the Timmins camp. An airborne geophysics programme is underway to refine drill targets at the E1, E1S, and E2 zones, followed by systematic stripping, channel sampling, and soil geochemistry designed to expand known gold-in-soil anomalies before drill testing in late Q3 to early Q4 2026. At the Acadian Gold Joint Venture in northern New Brunswick — one of Canada's emerging gold exploration jurisdictions following discoveries at nearby projects — a similar target-refinement programme is underway. Syenite-hosted gold is a distinct metallogeny from the more common Abitibi orogenic lode-gold systems; alkalic-style deposits in the Timmins region have produced significant mines in Canada. For retail investors tracking early-stage discovery stories: the combination of Timmins proximity and syenite geology provides a compelling discovery thesis ahead of the first drill holes, which are expected before year-end.

headline: COPPER HAS A TIMING PROBLEM AND EL DOMO IS RACING THE CLOCK — Why Almost No Copper Projects Will Deliver Before 2030, And Which One Can
snippet: A Yahoo Finance analysis examines the structural mismatch at the centre of the copper supply crisis: with the IEA's 2026 Critical Minerals Outlook placing the average time from copper discovery to first production at 17.2 years, virtually no project currently in exploration can deliver metal before 2040 — and even projects in feasibility study today face 8-10 years to production. Against this backdrop, El Domo (Silvercorp Metals, TSX: SVM) stands out as one of the very few large copper projects globally that is fully funded, fully permitted, and on a construction timeline targeting first production by July 2027. The project's updated construction budget of $284 million — revised from $240.5M due primarily to Ecuador's VAT rate, not cost overruns — is funded via a $175.5M Wheaton Precious Metals silver-gold stream and Silvercorp's $387M cash position from its operating Chinese silver mines. Annual production of 24 million pounds copper, 27,000 oz gold, 26 million pounds zinc and 529,000 oz silver makes El Domo a meaningful copper producer arriving precisely when the supply gap is widest. The copper timing problem — where the physical market tightens relentlessly while financial markets reward exploration companies whose projects are measured in decades, not years — makes construction-stage assets like El Domo categorically different from explorers in the same sector.

headline: J.P. MORGAN: GOLD'S LONGER-TERM CASE INTACT DESPITE WARSH PULLBACK — $6,300 VIEW MAINTAINED; Pullback From $4,626 Is Structural Accumulation Zone, Not Trend Change
snippet: J.P. Morgan Global Research, following the Warsh-driven gold pullback from $4,626 to $4,459 per ounce, affirmed its longer-term gold investment thesis and maintained its $6,300 per ounce price view on a 12-month forward basis. The bank characterises the pullback as structurally consistent with its bull case — rate sensitivity creating a tactical correction within a secular uptrend driven by USD reserve diversification, central bank purchasing (288.9 tonnes in Q2 2026), and fiscal deficit monetisation. The key analytical argument: gold has dropped approximately $20/oz for every 1 basis point rise in 10-year real yields since late February, confirming macro sensitivity — but the underlying structural demand from sovereign buyers is rate-insensitive and provides a floor that tactical corrections cannot erase. JPMorgan's Q4 2026 target of $4,500 per ounce has already been crossed by spot price on multiple occasions during August, validating the direction of travel even as near-term volatility around the September 4 NFP print and the September 15-16 FOMC creates a binary event risk. For retail investors: JPMorgan's $6,300 view, if correct, implies GDXJ — which roughly tripled gold's move in August — could reach levels not seen in the gold miner ETF's history, underscoring the importance of distinguishing between tactical pullback and structural trend.

headline: URANIUM MINERS MONTHLY AUGUST 2026: LONG-TERM PRICE NEARS $100/lb — Denison Phoenix ISR Construction Underway; Kazatomprom And Cameco On Track
snippet: HANetf's Uranium Miners Monthly Report for August 2026 documents a sector in bifurcated territory: uranium mining equities rebounded sharply during the month with both senior and junior groups recovering strongly year-to-date, even as spot uranium hovered near $89–90 per pound with long-term contract prices approaching $100 per pound — a term-above-spot premium that signals utility buyers are paying a forward premium for supply security rather than relying on spot availability. Key production developments: Denison Mines' Phoenix In-Situ Recovery uranium mine in Saskatchewan transitioned from site preparation to full-scale construction in late July, including initiation of the perimeter freeze wall installation for Phase 1 — a technically distinct ISR design with no direct US analogue. Kazatomprom and Cameco both confirmed they are on track for their full-year 2026 production targets. Kazatomprom's Tortkuduk-Zhalpak joint venture delay — which removed an estimated 77 million pounds from the forward supply schedule — remains the most significant near-term supply catalyst. The term-price premium, combined with utility undercontracting at approximately 30% of 10-year requirements versus the historical 70–80% norm, positions uranium for a sustained contracting cycle through 2027 that supports long-term price stability above $90.

headline: GOLD ENTERS SEPTEMBER TRAPPED BETWEEN $4,340 AND $4,730 MOVING AVERAGES — Analysts Split Between Goldman's $4,900, UBS's $5,200, And Bear-Case $4,000 Retest
snippet: Gold enters September in a technically ambiguous position — above the 200-day moving average at approximately $4,340 per ounce but below the 50-day moving average near $4,730, creating a 'no man's land' where neither bulls nor bears have definitive technical control. The September setup means the resolution will be data-driven: the five macro prints in the first week of September (JOLTS, ADP, ISM, PCE, August NFP on September 4) and the September 15-16 FOMC meeting are the catalysts that will resolve the technical uncertainty. Analyst targets span a wide range: Goldman Sachs at $4,900, Morgan Stanley and UBS at $5,200 on a 6-12 month view, JPMorgan's $4,500 Q4 target already crossed, and Long Forecast projecting a $4,750 September average with a high of $5,304 and a low of $4,136. The bear case — a retest of the $4,000 level — requires a September NFP significantly above the +80,000 consensus (which July's -23,000 print obliterated) and a subsequent repricing of rate hike probability above 65%. For retail investors in junior mining stocks: gold's position between its key moving averages means the September data gauntlet isn't just a macro event — it's the decision point that will determine whether August's record-breaking gold miner rally continues into Q4 or corrects before the junior capital rotation phase can fully develop.
